scope: G2 native DBOS source-installed library with real SQLite local system database; Python and TypeScript repositories count one project. No Postgres/cluster/power-loss claim.

cases.question: Confirmed step result survives process destruction without rerunning that step
cases.input: Workflow stable id flow-1, deterministic workflow calls step returning UUID plus fsynced count, then recv. Kill process after direct DB observation of step row; restart same version and send message
cases.oracle: Direct SQLite rows and independent count file show original UUID/step output retained, step executed once; final workflow uses that same result and explicit message. Old process absent before recovery.

cases.question: Same workflow identity with conflicting input
cases.input: After completed flow-1 repeat identity with different argument
cases.oracle: Observe actual result/error and direct stored input. Reusing old result without conflict error is a capability gap relative to our contract, even if documented idempotency succeeds.

cases.question: Sync wait still occupies per-workflow live resources
cases.input: Register three workflows waiting in DBOS.recv with stable IDs, inspect OS threads and captured thread stacks while waiting
cases.oracle: Count actual stacks through DBOS recv/Event.wait and OS thread IDs; do not call this zero merely because threads share one process. Once process killed its threads disappear but pending durable rows remain.

cases.question: Effect before step-result recording can repeat after crash
cases.input: Separate workflow step fsyncs effect log then waits at external gate before returning; SIGKILL before step result saved, restart with gate released
cases.oracle: Effect file line count and operation_outputs before/after reveal whether effect repeats. If repeats, reject naive DBOS-step wrapping for non-idempotent external effects; require explicit execution identity/query adapter.

execution: Only test-created files and SQLite; no models/remote effects. Every phase bounded30s, parent observes database/file/OS facts independently. Retain before/after database copies and logs, source/install/protocol hashes. Failed or missing observations remain FAIL; exactly-once external effects are not assumed.
